classification.difficultyReason: The student must find the hidden height by Pythagoras from the 13 cm side and 5 cm offset. They then substitute into the trapezium area formula and solve a linear equation for the unknown parallel side. This is two linked procedures with a modest reframing, and the diagram supplies the right angle.

content.prompt: Work out the length of the unknown side, if the area is $168\text{ cm}^2$.

answer.worked:
The dashed height, the $5\text{ cm}$ segment and the $13\text{ cm}$ side form a right triangle.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=13^2-5^2\\h^2&=144\\h&=12\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\168&=\frac{12(a+20)}{2}\\168&=6(a+20)\\28&=a+20\\a&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
